module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Mahler's 3/2 Problem

*Reference:* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahler%27s_3/2_problem)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Mahler32

/-- For a real number `α`, define `Ω(α)` as
$$
\Omega (\alpha )=\inf _{\theta > 0}\left({\limsup _{n\rightarrow \infty }\left\lbrace
{\theta \alpha ^{n}}\right\rbrace -\liminf _{n\rightarrow \infty }\left\lbrace {\theta \alpha ^{n}}\right\rbrace }\right).
$$
-/
noncomputable def Ω (α : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  sInf {Filter.atTop.limsup (fun n ↦ Int.fract (θ * α ^ n))
    - Filter.atTop.liminf (fun n ↦ Int.fract (θ * α ^ n)) | (θ : ℝ) (_ : 0 < θ)}

/-- The **Mahler Conjecture** states that there are no Z-numbers. -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem mahler_conjecture (x : ℝ) (hx : IsZNumber x) : False := by
  sorry

/-- Mahler's conjecture would follow if `Ω(3/2)` exceeded `1/2`: a Z-number `x` has all
fractional parts `{x (3/2)^n}` below `1/2`, so `Ω(3/2) ≤ 1/2`. -/
@[category textbook, AMS 11]
theorem mahler_conjecture.variants.consequence (H : 1 / 2 < Ω (3 / 2)) :
    type_of% mahler_conjecture := by
  sorry

/-- Flatto, Lagarias and Pollington proved that for all rational `p/q > 1` in lowest terms with
`q ≥ 2`, we have `Ω(p/q) ≥ 1/p`: for every `θ > 0`, the limit points of `{θ (p/q)^n}` are not
contained in any interval of length less than `1/p`. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem mahler_conjecture.variants.flatto_lagarias_pollington (p q : ℕ) (hq : 1 < q)
    (hpq : p.Coprime q) (hpq' : q < p) : 1 / p ≤ Ω (p / q) := by
  sorry

end Mahler32

reformulations.difference: The imported IsZNumber uses positive exponents n ≥ 1, matching Wikipedia. Mahler’s original paper instead requires the condition for n ≥ 0.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: These conventions give equivalent nonexistence statements. Any positive real satisfying the n ≥ 0 condition satisfies the n ≥ 1 condition. Conversely, if x satisfies the latter, y = x(3/2) satisfies the former, since y(3/2)^n = x(3/2)^(n+1). The omitted lower bound on fractional parts is automatic from Int.fract_nonneg. The equivalence of the full conjecture statements was proved in the scratch file.

reformulations.difference: The original paper’s Theorem 1.4 universally bounds the oscillation for each positive multiplier ξ; Lean packages these bounds as 1/p ≤ Ω(p/q).
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The set of oscillations over positive multipliers is nonempty and contained in [0,1]. Therefore c ≤ its real infimum is equivalent to every oscillation being at least c. Applying this with c = 1/p proves equivalence to Theorem 1.4. The paper also explicitly gives the Ω formulation on p. 130. The equivalence of the complete quantified statements was proved in Lean.

sources_consulted: K. Mahler, “An unsolved problem on the powers of 3/2,” Journal of the Australian Mathematical Society 8 (1968), 313–321, especially the definition on p. 313. https://doi.org/10.1017/S1446788700005371 ; full text: https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-cambridge-core/content/view/6416420BFE33A5DDC3DAB6EA358C2B0B/S1446788700005371a.pdf/an-unsolved-problem-on-the-powers-of-32.pdf

L. Flatto, J. C. Lagarias and A. D. Pollington, “On the range of fractional parts {ξ(p/q)^n},” Acta Arithmetica 70 (1995), 125–147, especially Theorem 1.4 and the Ω formulation on pp. 129–130, and its proof on pp. 138–139. https://doi.org/10.4064/aa-70-2-125-147 ; full text: https://www.impan.pl/shop/publication/transaction/download/product/108521
review.notes: Checked all four declarations; no mathematical defects or status issues found. Wikipedia displays a strict FLP bound and omits q ≥ 2, but the primary paper explicitly states the non-strict bound with coprime p > q ≥ 2, exactly as Lean does. This discrepancy is in Wikipedia, not the formalization. /workspace/review/scratch.lean compiles successfully and verifies boundedness/nonemptiness for Ω, representative boundary cases, real rather than natural division, both recorded equivalences, and the consequence theorem without relying on sorry-backed results.
